key_insight: Polarization switching in Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 occurs through a dynamic cooperative exchange between O3c and O4c oxygen atoms, not by simple ion displacement.
engineering_relevance: This atomistic mechanism explains how HZO can switch robustly with little macroscopic strain, informing ferroelectric memory designs that prioritize stable cooperative pathways for endurance and scaling.
method: Electric-field-induced molecular dynamics simulations on a defect-free ideal HZO lattice
Machine-learning interatomic force field (MACEField) to capture switching dynamics
Trajectory analysis of oxygen coordination changes and transient bond formation
evidence_signal: The simulations dynamically reproduced the P-E hysteresis loop and revealed a detour pathway plus internal self-compensation during switching.
watch_item: The study uses an ideal defect-free lattice, so real-device defects, interfaces, and processing variability may alter the switching pathway.
paper_title: Transient Detour and Cooperative Oxygen Exchange in the Polarization Switching of Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2
